description.en: Palestine with Phoenicia and Coele Syria, which Ptolemy's general Nicanor took from the satrap Laomedon c. 319/318 BCE (Diodorus).
description.ar: فلسطين مع فينيقيا وسوريا المجوّفة، التي انتزعها نيكانور قائد بطليموس من الوالي لاوميدون نحو 319/318 ق.م. (ديودوروس).
description.he: פלשתינה עם פיניקיה וסוריה החלולה, שנקנור, מצביאו של תלמי, נטל מידי הסטרפ לאומדון בערך ב־319/318 לפנה״ס (דיודורוס).

sources.quote: After the death of Alexander in 323 bce, Palestine, with much of Syria and Phoenicia, fell to Ptolemy I (Soter)
Syria to Laomedon of Mitylenê, Cilicia to Philotas
He gave Syria to Laomedon of Mitylenê and Cilicia to Philoxenus.
Seeing that Phoenicia and Coelê Syria, as it was called, were conveniently situated for an offensive against Egypt, he set about in earnest to become master of those regions.
The latter marched into Syria, took the satrap Laomedon captive, and subdued the whole land.
For Ptolemy's campaign in Syria cp. Marmor Parium for 319/18;

notes.en: Actual Ptolemaic occupation in these years was intermittent; see antigonid-realm.
notes.ar: كان الاحتلال البطلمي الفعلي في هذه السنوات متقطعًا؛ انظر antigonid-realm.
notes.he: הכיבוש התלמי בפועל בשנים אלה היה לסירוגין; ראו antigonid-realm.

description.en: Palestine and Phoenicia; northern frontier apparently just north of Tripoli on the Eleutherus (Nahr al-Kabir); Philadelphia (Rabbath Ammon) bore a Ptolemaic dynastic name.
description.ar: فلسطين وفينيقيا؛ الحد الشمالي على ما يبدو شمال طرابلس مباشرة عند الإلوثروس (النهر الكبير)؛ وحملت فيلادلفيا (ربّة عمّون) اسمًا أسريًا بطلميًا.
description.he: פלשתינה ופיניקיה; הגבול הצפוני כנראה מעט צפונית לטריפולי על האלפתרוס (נהר אל-כביר); פילדלפיה (רבת עמון) נשאה שם שושלתי תלמי.

sources.quote: The northern boundary of the kingdom established by Ptolemy lay apparently slightly north of modern Tripoli, Lebanon, perhaps on the course of the Kabīr River (ancient Eleutherus)
At Panion, on the northern boundary of Galilee, the armies of Antiochus and Ptolemy met, and Ptolemy was defeated.
But Ptolemy had already occupied the cities of that region
The root cause of the wars was the occupation of Koile Syria by Ptolemy I in 301 BC
This is an area which in the 3rd century BC was ruled by the Ptolemies

notes.en: Temporary Seleucid occupation during the Fourth Syrian War (before Raphia, 217) not modelled.
notes.ar: لم يُمثَّل الاحتلال السلوقي المؤقت خلال الحرب السورية الرابعة (قبل رفح، 217).
notes.he: הכיבוש הסלאוקי הזמני במהלך מלחמת סוריה הרביעית (לפני רפיח, 217) לא מודל.

description.en: After Panion only the possessions south of the Sinai desert edge (Egypt incl. Sinai) remained Ptolemaic in the map area.
description.ar: بعد بانياس لم يبق بطلميًا في منطقة الخريطة إلا ما جنوب حافة صحراء سيناء (مصر بما فيها سيناء).
description.he: לאחר פאניון נותרו תלמיים באזור המפה רק הרכוש שמדרום לשולי מדבר סיני (מצרים כולל סיני).

sources.quote: Thus, the Ptolemaic possessions north of the Sinai desert, including Palestine, passed into the hands of the house of Seleucus.
When Scopas was conquered by Antiochus, that king occupied Samaria, Abila, and Gadara
in the 2nd century BC mostly was controlled by the Seleucids
